results.summary: This design implements a host-driven primitive engine for transformer layers, featuring a 2x2 systolic array of multiply-accumulate processing elements with signed 5-bit operands and 11-bit results. The interface allows a host to write operands and commands, and read results one word at a time. No external hardware is required beyond a standard Tiny Tapeout board or simulator, and the design is notable for its compact implementation of a systolic schedule.

This design implements an 8-bit ALU with a state machine that reads two 8-bit operands via the digital input pins. Operation selection and status output are provided over the bidirectional pins. The ALU supports basic arithmetic and logic operations. It is tested using a standard Tiny Tapeout board or simulator.

This project implements a 4x4 systolic array matrix multiply-accumulate (MAC) accelerator in SystemVerilog. It performs matrix multiplication with accumulation. The design is intended for digital signal processing or machine learning applications. It is verified using a standard testbench.

tcpu is an 8-bit CPU with integrated IO and a bootloader, featuring a simple instruction set that includes add, and, not, jump, store, load, and nop operations. It uses a UART interface for programming and communication, requiring an external USB-to-UART converter. The CPU is designed for educational purposes and can be tested on a Tiny Tapeout board. Its notable feature is the integrated bootloader for easy program loading.

This design is an analog sensor interface that includes an oscillator and RF components. It is intended for instrumentation applications. The design uses analog circuitry to interface with sensors. It is tested using standard Tiny Tapeout analog test methods.

The design includes a controller, register file, and a combinational MAC array that computes the full matmul in a single cycle. This will be useful if it turns out that the silicon is too slow to work at the intended 50.4 MHz clock frequency. The design is a matrix multiply accelerator. It is tested using a standard testbench.

This design is a music synthesizer with audio output and VGA graphics. It includes a sequencer and uses PWM and sigma-delta techniques for sound generation. The design is intended for demoscene or retro applications. It is tested using a standard Tiny Tapeout board with audio and VGA connections.

This design is a game that uses VGA output and gamepad input. It features graphics and audio. The game is implemented in a retro style. It is tested using a standard Tiny Tapeout board with VGA and gamepad connections.

This design is an 8-bit CPU with a simple instruction set. It includes a register file and a bus interface. The CPU is intended for educational purposes. It is tested using a standard Tiny Tapeout board.

This design is a hardware accelerator for matrix multiplication. It uses a systolic array architecture. The accelerator is intended for machine learning applications. It is tested using a standard testbench.
